name: John Scott Harrison

death.place: Point Farm, near North Bend, Hamilton Co., Ohio

burial.cemetery: Harrison family tomb (William Henry Harrison Tomb State Memorial)

events.title: U.S. House of Representatives
events.description: Elected as a Whig in 1852, re-elected in 1854 as an Anti-Nebraska candidate; defeated for a third term in 1856 and retired to Point Farm.

events.title: Body stolen by grave robbers and found at the Ohio Medical College
events.description: Despite a deep brick-lined grave, cemented stones and a hired watchman, his body was taken the night after burial. His son John Harrison and grandson George Eaton, searching the Ohio Medical College for the stolen body of a young neighbour (Augustus Devin), found Harrison's body hanging by the neck in a chute; the janitor was arrested.

bioAdditions:
John Scott Harrison (4 Oct 1804 - 25 May 1878) was a son of President William Henry Harrison and Anna Tuthill Symmes, born at Grouseland, Vincennes, and the father of President Benjamin Harrison; he is the only American who was both son and father of a president (S1). He studied law but farmed at Point Farm, North Bend, Ohio, and served two terms in Congress (1853-57), first as a Whig and then as an Anti-Nebraska man. He married (1) Lucretia Knapp Johnson in 1824 (three children) and (2) on 12 Aug 1831 Elizabeth Ramsey Irwin (1810-1850), daughter of Archibald Irwin and Mary Ramsey, with whom he had ten children, including Benjamin (S1).

He died suddenly at home in May 1878. The New York Herald of 31 May 1878 carried the Cincinnati telegraph story: the family had seen that a neighbour's grave had been robbed and took 'extraordinary precautions', yet the body was stolen; his son John and grandson George Eaton, searching the Ohio Medical College with a warrant for the other body, hauled up a corpse on a rope and recognised it ('My God, it's father!'). The scandal fed into Ohio's 1881 anatomy law (S2, S1).
funFacts: Only man in U.S. history to be both the son and the father of a president.
The contemporary Herald report says it was his son John (Jr.) with grandson George Eaton who found the body; later retellings often credit Benjamin.
